note: Registry of pre-auth surfaces for the enumeration-boundary parity harness (test/example/test/example_web/enumeration_parity_test.exs). A row with state parity proves ONLY the listed dimensions for the exact request sequence described in that row; most rows cover one request, while repeat-attempt and rate-limit rows specify their sequence. Nothing here proves timing equivalence or behavior for account states not named in the row. The harness runs in the example host, a hand-maintained copy of the generated host that already drifts from the generated templates; only install_smoke proves a generated host. States: parity (must compare same), known_divergence (must still differ; fixing the product forces this row to be removed or changed), by_design (documented behaviour is asserted), not_proven (no assertion; blocker cites the file:line that prevents a deterministic probe). The compare lists of the five named rows are pinned in the parity test to the dimensions the published docs rely on (the account-existence rows keep status, redirect, flash and body): a row may list more, never fewer.

surfaces.note: Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One failed attempt (wrong password) for an existing email versus any password for an unknown email, fresh state: no earlier failures, account not locked. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Repeat attempts (lockout), timing and the locked and unconfirmed states are NOT compared; see password-signin-repeat-attempts.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One magic-link request for an existing email versus an unknown email, fresh state. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Email delivery (presence and subject), timing and the library rate limit are NOT compared; see magic-link-rate-limit.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One reset request submitted through the LiveView form for an existing email versus an unknown email, fresh state. Compares the reported redirect outcome (302), the redirect location, the flash read from the redirect and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. NOT compared: response timing (an unknown address costs one dummy hash, an existing one writes a token and delivers an email), email delivery, the rate limit (see password-reset-rate-limit), locked, unconfirmed and enterprise-policy accounts, and the generated host (the example host is a hand-maintained copy; this parity row does not compare it). A separate generated-host install-smoke probe mounts the generated request page and submits existing and unknown addresses, checking the same redirect and flash plus one token only for the existing address; it does not measure timing or extend this row's parity claim.

Identity = the email an anonymous visitor puts in the resend event payload: an existing, still-unconfirmed account versus an address never stored. The resend handler takes its target from the session user and ignores the payload, so this row proves a visitor-supplied identity is ignored, not that an email-keyed resend form exists: no email-keyed resend form exists in the example or in the generated page, and nothing here covers one. One anonymous resend event with the email in its payload, fresh state. Compares the reported redirect outcome (302), the redirect location, the flash read from the redirect (an error asking the visitor to log in), the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email, and the number of confirmation tokens created for that email (zero for both). NOT compared: a signed-in visitor's own resend (the session owner's account, not an enumeration channel), response timing, rate limits, or the code-entry path. This row is example-host evidence only; a separate generated-host install-smoke probe covers LiveView confirmation plus the generated controller actions, and a generator contract test checks the --no-live routes stay outside the authenticated-user redirect pipeline. This row proves a payload email is ignored and is counted separately from the account-existence surfaces (password-signin, magic-link-request, password-reset-request) by the named-surface rule in the parity test; it can never satisfy or substitute for them.

Identity = code kind, not account existence: for a user with an MFA-pending session, one wrong authenticator code (existing) versus one wrong backup code (unknown), each on a freshly enrolled user. Compares the outcome (re-rendered in place, reported as 200), redirect location and the flash message including the remaining-attempts count. The flash is read from the LiveView process state because the view does not render it in its own markup. The body is NOT compared: the authenticator and backup panels differ by design. A pending versus absent MFA session and the lockout outcome are NOT compared. This row is counted separately from the account-existence surfaces (password-signin, magic-link-request, password-reset-request) by the named-surface rule in the parity test and can never satisfy or substitute for them.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account, over repeated attempts. After the configured lockout threshold, the library returns the same invalid_credentials result and safe message for a locked existing account and an unknown email; lockout details remain in audit and telemetry. The example sign-in controller also returns the same response. The probe compares the library result after the configured number of wrong-password attempts; timing and other account states are not compared.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account (existing = duplicate registration, unknown = new registration). Known divergence, asserted: a new email sets the auto-sign-in trigger (phx-trigger-action on the form, no flash) while a duplicate email re-renders with only an info flash. The difference is inherent to signing a new account in and remains visible regardless of the duplicate flash text. For valid submissions, both paths hash the password before the database accepts or rejects the insert; the test proves the hash is computed on the duplicate path, but this row does not measure timing or claim wall-clock equality. See the registration guide for this boundary.

Identity = whether the invitee email already has an account. By design the invitation URL is a capability: an anonymous visitor with a valid token sees the same signup branch whether or not the invitee already has an account, and the invitee email shown on the page is part of the capability (normalized as the echoed email). Reading identity parity onto a capability URL is an interpretation. The invalid, expired, revoked, mismatch and signed-in branches are NOT compared.

Passkey-primary options are discoverable and do not accept an account identifier. Existing and unknown email payloads return the same status and top-level JSON keys; both expose an empty allowCredentials list, asserted by the passkey controller test. Per-request challenges differ and are not compared.

Identity = whether the submitted work email belongs to an account. By design discovery answers per email DOMAIN: two addresses on one connected domain, one registered and one not, get the identical redirect and flash, while a domain without an active connection gets a different answer (the domain, not the user, is what is revealed). The SSO page the redirect lands on is not followed or compared.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account when a configured limiter denies the request. The parity probe submits a real existing account and an unknown address through Sigra.Auth.request_magic_link/3 with the same denying limiter; both return the rate-limited result before account lookup. The result is the only compared dimension. Unthrottled token return values, timing and the production limiter policy are not compared.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account when a configured limiter denies the request. The parity probe submits a real existing account and an unknown address through Sigra.Auth.request_password_reset/3 with the same denying limiter; both return the rate-limited result before account lookup. The result is the only compared dimension. Unthrottled token return values, timing and the production limiter policy are not compared.
